Applicant must identify the probable users and end‑users of the technology resulting from the research.
Applicant must not seek funding for foreign travel, salaries of regular employees of the institute, or honorariums for investigators.
Applicant must not utilize the grant for construction, maintenance, or repair of buildings, or for the purchase of vehicles and air conditioners.
Applicant must complete any previous ongoing research projects funded by the Ministry of Water Resources before submitting a new research proposal.
Applicant must be an Indian citizen to be eligible for research fellowships and associateships.
Applicant must be a brilliant Indian scientist or engineer.
Applicant must be residing/working abroad at the time of nomination and intend to return to India.
Applicant must possess a higher degree such as a Ph.D. in Science/Engineering, Master in Engineering/Technology, or MD in Medicine (or equivalent).
Applicant must have adequate professional experience.
Applicant must have a proven/outstanding track record as evidenced by research publications and recognitions.
Applicant must not hold any permanent, tenure-track, or contractual position in any Indian Institute/University at the time of nomination.
Nominations from the applicant's Ph.D. guide or from the same institute where the Ph.D. was obtained will not be considered.
The fellowship must be taken up in a new area or laboratory different from where the applicant obtained their doctorate degree.

Applicant must be a regularly appointed faculty member working in an institution that is either: a university (including constituent/affiliated colleges) under Section 2(f) of the UGC Act, 1956 with valid NAAC accreditation; a deemed university under Section 3 of the UGC Act 1956 with valid NAAC accreditation; an institution fully funded by Central or State Government empowered to award degrees; or an Institution of National Importance.
Applicant must have a minimum of 10 years of service remaining in the university from the date of application.
Applicant must have successfully supervised a Ph.D. dissertation of at least 5 full-time candidates.
Applicant must have successfully completed at least 2 sponsored research projects funded by national or international government or private agencies.
Must be pursuing full-time M.Phil/Ph.D. research without holding a JRF from UGC-NET or UGC-CSIR NET.
Author must be a citizen of India
Book must be an original work in Hindi (translated books not eligible)

Book must fall within specified genres: Engineering, Electronics, Computer Science, Physics, Biology, Energy, Space Science, Medicine, Chemistry, Information Technology, Management, Psychology, Liberalisation, Globalisation, Consumerism, Human Rights, Pollution, Forensic Science, Police, Criminology Research, Police Administration, Culture, Religion, Arts and Heritage, Law-related subjects
Each co-author must submit a separate application
Books previously awarded by any government organization are ineligible; author must disclose any other award before declaration
Only books published between 1 January and 31 December of the year are eligible
Book must be an analytical review; theses, poems, novels, stories, plays, or textbooks are not eligible
Author responsible for facts and figures, must provide references where possible
Applicant must not have received a prize under any Department of Official Language scheme in the preceding three years (co‑authors may still participate proportionally)
Book must contain at least 100 pages
Only books with an ISBN are accepted

Preferred academic disciplines include Public Policy Studies, Social Policy Studies, Development Studies, Economics, Governance and Public Administration Studies, Rural Development Management, Business Administration, Environment and Energy Studies, Public Health Studies, Sociology, Political Science, Social Work, Statistics, Data Analysis, and other relevant Social Sciences, Management, and Engineering streams (preference, not mandatory).
Internship duration must be at least 15 days and not exceed six months; note that an exclusion states the period shall be at least four weeks but not exceeding three months.
Interns must have their own laptop.
Candidates who do not expect a stipend/honorarium may join on a pro bono basis with approval of the Division Head.
Interns who do not complete the requisite period will not be issued any certificate.
The deceased worker must be employed in an establishment registered under the Factories Act, 1948.
The deceased worker's monthly salary (basic + DA) must not exceed ₹15,000.
Application must be made within one year of the worker's date of death.
Financial assistance is payable to the worker's spouse, or dependent son/unmarried daughter, or parents if the worker was unmarried.
Applicant must be an Indian scientist working in agriculture or allied fields in ICAR institutes, public agricultural institutions, or Krishi Vigyan Kendras.
Applicant must have made significant contributions in agriculture or allied sciences with clear and proven impact on society, economy, or environment, supported by the Head of the Institution.
Applicant must have a clean service record with no pending enquiry or major punishment in the last five years.
Applicant may submit only one application per year for a given contribution.
Applicant must apply under only one award category.
For innovation/research awards (individual or team up to five members), applicant must be below 60 years of age.
For interdisciplinary research, applicant must be part of a team of at least three members from different disciplines and the team leader must be below 60 years of age.
For women scientist category, applicant must be a woman and below 60 years of age.
For young scientist category, applicant must hold a doctoral degree, hold a regular position, and be below 45 years of age.
Applicant must have 10th pass with science and knowledge of computer
Applicant/entrepreneur group must have own premises or rented building with lease agreement for at least four years
Applicant must be a Manufacturing or Service MSME with a valid Udyam Registration Certificate.
Trading activity is not permitted under the scheme.
Applicant must be a non-pensioner ex-serviceman or his widow.
Must be of rank Havildar/equivalent and below.
Must be recommended by respective Zila Sainik Board (ZSB).
Expenditure must be incurred at recognized government hospitals at rates approved under CGHS/ECHS.
Applicant must be an ex-serviceman or the widow of an ex-serviceman.
Child must be a legitimate offspring of the ex-serviceman or widow.
Ex-serviceman must hold the rank of Junior Commissioned Officer (JCO) or equivalent in the Navy/Air Force or a lower rank.
Child must have 100% disability.
Child must not be receiving any disability benefit from any official agency.
Application must be recommended by the respective Zila Sainik Board (ZSB).
Applicant must be an ex-serviceman, widow, or orphan dependent.
Must be of rank Havildar or equivalent and below.
Must not be receiving any education allowance or similar benefit from the State or employer.
Scheme is limited to the first two children; twin exceptions apply as described.
In case of demise of the 1st or 2nd child, subsequent children become eligible as per discharge book.
The ward or widow must complete the course successfully.
Applicant must be a legitimate offspring of an Ex‑Serviceman with details recorded in the Service Book.
Applicant must be either a son below 21 years of age or an unmarried daughter.
Applicant must have lost both parents (the Ex‑Serviceman and spouse).
Application must be recommended by the respective Zila Sainik Board (ZSB).
Must be a non-pensioner Ex-Serviceman (ESM) or his widow.
Rank must be Havildar/equivalent or below (Navy/Air Force).

ESM/widow must be 65 years of age on 01 April of the financial year of application, except widows of ESM who were already receiving the Penury Grant at the time of the ESM's death (age condition waived).
Ex-Servicemen receiving a pension are not eligible.
Applicant must be widow of an Ex-Serviceman (ESM) of rank up to Havildar or equivalent
Applicant must have successfully completed the vocational training
Applicant must be recommended by the respective Zila Sainik Board (ZSB)
Applicant must represent a Micro and Small Enterprise (MSE).
The deceased must have been aged between 18 and 59 years
The deceased must have belonged to a Below Poverty Line (BPL) household
The deceased must have been the primary breadwinner of the family
Applicant must be a citizen of Sri Lanka.
Applicant must be a victim of the upsurge of ethnic violence in Sri Lanka.
Refugees who arrive by air, seek permission from the Director of Rehabilitation to stay with relatives, and are referred by the Director to the local police officer for registration are not eligible.

Applicant must be a retired scientist, engineer, or technologist from units of the Department of Atomic Energy (including aided institutions). Must have rich experience in the selected research area, possess domain knowledge related to the selected topic, and have expertise in the area of the topic selected for the award.
Applicant must be an Indian national working overseas in life sciences, biotechnology, bio-engineering, healthcare, agriculture/veterinary biotechnology, bio-energy or allied areas.
Must have at least three years of post-doctoral research experience in overseas research laboratories (required for M.Tech pathway; expected for PhD/MD pathway).
Those who have returned to India within one year of the advertisement closing date are eligible; women candidates have a two-year window.
Applicants who have secured a permanent position in India within the aforementioned return period are not eligible.
Applicants must have a proven/outstanding track record evidenced by research publications and recognitions.
Applicant must be a professional/research institution/organization.
Applicant must be engaged in the field of official statistics for at least three years.
Applicant must have qualified statisticians, economists, and social scientists.

Applicant must fall into one of: government institutions (including State/UT Directorates of Economics and Statistics); institutions receiving annual recurring grants from Central/State Govt agencies (e.g., ISI, CSIR, UGC); societies registered under Societies Registration Act; trusts registered under Trusteeship Act; companies incorporated under Companies Act.
For seminar/conference/workshop assistance, applicant must be not‑for‑profit.
For travel grant assistance (officials), applicant must be an official of Central Government/Central autonomous institutions/university.
Visit must relate to officer’s area of work.
Technical paper must be submitted through proper official channel, not voluntarily.
Must have official invitation from host organization to administrative Ministry/Department/Organization.
Must have documentary evidence of paper acceptance by organizing agency.
Must have obtained all necessary clearances, including political clearance from MEA and FCRA clearance from MHA where required.
Must not have had more than one travel‑grant proposal recommended in the same financial year.

Exclusions: no assistance for pure theoretical research proposals; no assistance for annual meetings of statistical associations/societies; no capital expenditure; salary of Project Director/Experts if regular employee cannot be charged to project cost.
Applicant must be a professional in journalism (newspaper/magazine/radio/TV), civil society, or research and training in RTI.
Applicant must have proven credentials in their professional area.
Applicant must have prior experience of work relating to the Right to Information.
Applicant must have an aptitude for research.
Applicant must be a scientist, technologist, or innovator working in government or private organization.
Must have contributed pathbreaking research, technology-led innovation, or discovery in any field of science, or developed innovative technologies with significant societal impact.
Scientists, technologists, and innovators of Indian origin abroad with exceptional contributions benefitting Indian communities or society at large are also eligible.

Work must fall within one of the 13 specified domains: Physics, Chemistry, Biological Sciences, Mathematics & Computer Science, Earth Science, Medicine, Engineering Sciences, Agricultural Science, Environmental Science, Technology & Innovation, Atomic Energy, Space Science and Technology, Others.
Must be an Indian citizen.
Must not have received assistance for the same purpose in the last 3 years; for children below 12 years, at least 1 year must have elapsed since last assistance.
Must be a resident of Bihar.
Must be admitted to the first year of a degree course or the second year via lateral entry in an AICTE‑approved institution.
The gap between passing the qualifying examination and admission must not exceed two years.
Student must be promoted to the next class/level each year; otherwise the scholarship is forfeited.
If the candidate drops out or fails in a subsequent year, further scholarship is not granted.
Must not receive any other financial assistance, scholarship, salary, stipend, etc. during the course; otherwise the scholarship is discontinued and the amount must be refunded.
Candidate must be admitted to the first year of a diploma course or the second year via lateral entry in an AICTE‑approved institution.
The gap between the year of passing the qualifying examination and the session of admission in the diploma course must not exceed two years.
Students who fail to get promoted to the next class/level forfeit the scholarship.
If a candidate fails or drops out in a subsequent year, they are not eligible for further scholarship.

The student must not receive any other financial assistance (scholarship, stipend, salary, emoluments, etc.) from any other source during the course of study; otherwise the scholarship will be discontinued and the full amount must be refunded.

Applicant must be an organization/institution of one of the following types: a society registered under the Indian Societies Registration Act, 1860; a charitable non-profit-making company; a public trust registered under any law; a registered non-official organization engaged in social welfare; or a university, research institute, school, statutory body (e.g., Panchayati Raj Institutions, Municipal Corporations, Town Area Committees, Red Cross Societies and their branches).
The organization must have at least two years of experience working in the related area or demonstrate competence to undertake the proposed scheme.
The organization must not be operated for profit for any individual or body of individuals.
The organization must have a properly constituted Managing Body with its powers, duties, and responsibilities clearly defined and laid down in a written constitution.

Applicant must be one of the following institutions: Indian Institute of Public Administration, Administrative Staff College of India, Indian Institute/s of Management, Indian Law Institute, National Law University, National Council of Applied Economic Research, National Judicial Academy, State Judicial Academy.
Applicant must be working in one of the following fields: Justice Delivery, Legal Education and Research, Judicial Reforms.
For senior fellowship, applicant must be above 40 years of age; for junior fellowship, applicant must be between 25 and 40 years of age (inclusive). Age is reckoned as of 1st April of the year.
Graduation (bachelor's degree) is the minimum educational qualification.
Senior fellowship applicants must not be recipients of pension from the Ministry of Culture under the scheme for grant of financial assistance to artists in indigent circumstances.
Applicants must not have previously availed the same fellowship; however, a former Junior Fellow may apply for Senior Fellowship if at least 5 years have elapsed since closure of the earlier project.
The fellowship is not intended for providing training, conducting workshops, seminars, documenting memoirs, writing autobiographies, fiction, etc.
Household must not have had a functional toilet before the scheme.
Household must not possess a functional toilet at the time of application.
Household must not have a toilet.
Household must be located in a village.
Household must not have previously received any benefit for toilet construction under any other government programme.
Household must not have access to an individual household latrine or must have an insanitary toilet.
Must be enrolled at an Anganwadi Centre and receiving pre‑school education there.

Applicant must be a public trust, society, body corporate, organization, or institution covered under section 10(23BBA) or 12AA of the Income Tax Act, or a company under section 8 of the Companies Act 2013/section 25 of 1956, or a public trust/society registered under respective laws, for charitable/religious purposes.
Must be involved in charitable/religious activities by free and philanthropic distribution of food/prasad/langar/bhandara without discrimination.
Must have been in existence for the preceding three years before applying.
Must have been distributing free food, langar, and prasad to the public for at least the past three years on the day of application (self‑certificate required).
Must not be receiving any financial assistance from Central/State Government for the purpose of distributing free food.
Must serve free food to at least 5,000 people in a calendar month.
Must not be blacklisted under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) or any Central/State Government Act/Rules.
Institute must be AICTE-approved Government/Government-aided engineering college, university department, or polytechnic.
Institute must have been in existence for at least five years.
For CAFES SC/ST students: at least 200 SC/ST students on roll.
For CAFES NER: at least 60 students from NER per year.
For CAFES Differently Abled: at least 150 differently-abled students on roll.
Annual Progress Report must be submitted within 2 months of completion of the year.
After project completion, a Project Completion Report must be submitted.
Utilization Certificate and Statement of Accounts in prescribed proforma duly audited by the Finance Officer/Account Officer are required.
If construction work is not initiated within six months, the amount must be refunded to AICTE with accrued interest and justification.
Any change in the construction plan leading to a reduction in facilities or area is not allowed.

Applicant must be an Indian national individual or institution (including voluntary organizations, corporate entities, academic institutions, or uniformed forces) registered in India, and must have demonstrated work and achievements in disaster management including prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, relief, rehabilitation, research, saving lives, reducing impact on lives/livelihoods/property, mobilizing resources, undertaking immediate relief work, using technology innovatively, working on disaster mitigation in hazard‑prone areas, contributing to community capacity building and awareness, developing or supporting early warning systems, and contributing to research, innovation, and rehabilitation efforts.
Must be a national-level association or organisation.
Should have been in existence for at least 2 years.
Must be registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 if privately funded.
Professional associations/organisations of social scientists, companies and trusts should have been involved in national/regional/local socio-economic research objectives.
Must submit annual reports, audited accounts, and member lists for the past three years.
Exclusions: Organisations not engaged in academic activities in social sciences.
Exclusions: Associations working only in extension/welfare work.
Must have valid Udyam Registration.
Applicant must be sole proprietorship, partnership, co-operative, private or public limited company owned by SC/ST entrepreneur.
Business must be in manufacturing or service sector.
SC/ST units must have graduated from small to medium scale within 3 years of graduation.
New industries graduating to medium scale due to loan are eligible.
Cannot simultaneously receive another subsidy for the same plant & machinery/equipment under any other central/state scheme.
Fabricated or second-hand machinery is not eligible.
Applicant must be a citizen/resident of Uttar Pradesh.
Disability certificate must be issued by Chief Medical Officer or Doctor of Community Health Centre/Primary Health Centre.
Applicant must not have any criminal or financial convictions and no government dues payable.
Applicant must own or be able to acquire at least 110 sq ft of land for shop construction.
Applicant must agree to provide a 5-year tenure lease to a tenant for shop operation (including rent and working capital).
Annual income must not exceed twice the government-prescribed poverty line limit.

Eligible if: (a) Indian citizen aged above 60 years; or (b) Indian citizen aged 55‑60 years who has opted for Voluntary Retirement Scheme or Superannuation; or (c) retired defense personnel aged above 50 and below 60 years. Investment must be made within one month of receiving retirement benefits for categories (b) and (c).

College must offer minimum 4-5 UG courses in basic science and 1-2 applied/PG diploma courses; must have adequate in-house faculty expertise; independent labs for practicals; lecture halls with capacity for sanctioned student strength; basic infrastructure including LCD/projection, computers with internet; must be Government or Government-aided, autonomous college under Section 2(f)/12(B) of UGC Act 1956; colleges previously not recommended can re-apply after modifications; colleges discontinued after support can re-apply only after a 2-year cooling period; colleges already supported can apply for additional department after completion of one cycle (3 years) of ongoing support.
The applicant must be a College.
The applicant must be included in the list of Colleges maintained by the University Grants Commission.
The applicant must be included under Sections 2(f) and 12B of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956.
Applicant must be an Indian citizen aged at least 17 years.
Applicant can be an unskilled worker or a professional seeking upskilling or reskilling.
Applicant can be an undergraduate student or personnel working in technical textile fields.
Exact age and qualification requirements may vary depending on the specific training program.

Applicant must be studying in Class 9 or above, or a school dropout from 8th pass onwards, or hold an ITI certificate, diploma, undergraduate, graduate degree, or be registered in employment exchanges.
Must possess a valid Aadhaar number or Aadhaar Enrolment ID (EID).
Must provide consent for Aadhaar authentication or e-KYC process.
Must not have previously benefited from any Government of India‑aided skilling course in the ESDM sector (Central or State sponsored).
Must submit an undertaking declaring non‑availment of any such scheme at the time of enrolment.
Must be willing to get employed or self‑employed and submit an undertaking to that effect.
Must attend at least 70% of the training sessions to be eligible for assessment.
The benefit can be availed only once; for manufacturing job roles a second successive NSQF‑level course may be allowed.
Reservation: 60% of seats for General Category, 40% for Reserved Categories (SC 15%, ST 7.5%, EWS 17.5%).
For EWS category, the applicant’s family income must not exceed ₹2,00,000 per annum.
Applicant must be a student pursuing a full-time MBA/MCA or equivalent two‑year diploma, OR hold a full‑time graduate degree in Engineering or BCA.
Minimum 60% aggregate marks (or equivalent CGPA) required at graduate level.
Strong aptitude for computer programming and data analytics expected.
Applicant must be an Indian citizen.
Internship open to students of institutes based in and around Mumbai.
Applicant must have their own laptop for the internship.
Applicant must maintain a regular schedule and demonstrate professionalism.
Applicant must sign a non-disclosure agreement to protect SECI's data.
Applicant must be enrolled in a recognized institution in India or abroad.
Must not be availing any similar benefits from central or state government schemes.
Must have secured the minimum marks in the qualifying examination for the targeted competitive exam as per its guidelines.

Must have passed Class 12th or be studying in Class 12th for exams requiring Class 12 qualification; OR must have completed a bachelor's degree or be studying in the final year of a bachelor's degree for exams requiring graduation qualification.
Can avail the scheme benefits a maximum of two times in lifetime.

Must be undertaking one of the following activities: setting up grain-based distilleries/expansion using dry milling technique to produce DDGS; setting up new molasses-based distilleries/expansion with Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD); setting up new dual feed distilleries or expanding existing dual feed distilleries; converting existing molasses-based or grain-based distilleries to dual feed; setting up distilleries from other feedstocks producing 1G ethanol (sugar beet, sorghum, cereals, etc.); installing Molecular Sieve Dehydration (MSDH) column to convert rectified spirit to ethanol in existing distilleries.
Applicant must hold a Bachelor’s degree in Law from a Bar Council of India recognised institution (final-year law students are also eligible).
Age must be between 20 and 32 years inclusive.
Applicant must not be engaged in any other employment or assignment.
Applicant must not have been involved in any criminal case (pending or convicted) for an offence involving moral turpitude.
Applicant must not be facing any disciplinary proceeding before any Bar Council, institute or other authority.
Applicant must possess research and analytical skills, good writing ability, and knowledge of computers and legal research tools (e.g., eSCR, SCC Online, Manupatra, LexisNexis, Westlaw).
Applicant must be an Indian citizen.
Must have an established publication record in reputed journals or books.
Must be affiliated with a UGC-recognized or ICSSR research institute.
Should not be availing any other fellowship concurrently.
Must not be a defaulter of ICSSR funds.
Must not be receiving any other government fellowships during the tenure.
Applicants must be Indian citizens.
Applicants must hold a regular academic/research position in a recognized academic institution, national laboratory, or other recognized R&D institution in India.

Faculties recruited through the UGC-Faculty Recharge Program, INSPIRE Faculty, Ramanujan Fellows, and Ramalingaswamy Fellows are eligible if they have at least three and a half years of tenure remaining.
A female co‑PI from the same institute is mandatory; male co‑PIs are not allowed.
The PhD guide of the applicant cannot serve as a co‑PI.
Principal investigators who have previously received a POWER Grant are not eligible to apply again.
JC Bose fellows and PIs who have already completed two CRG grants are not eligible.
The number of co‑PIs per project must not exceed two.
Budget under the equipment head is limited to not more than ₹14 lakhs for Tier II institutions (₹30 lakhs limit).
Must be an awardee of INSPIRE Faculty (DST) or Ramanujan Fellowship (SERB).
Must have completed or be nearing completion of the tenure of the respective fellowship.
The scheme can be availed only once in a candidate's career.
Host institution must be in India (recognized academic institution, national laboratory, or recognized R&D institution) and provide administrative/infrastructural support.
SRS cannot be implemented in the same department/institution where the candidate earned their PhD/M.S./M.D.
Assignment is temporary/contractual for up to 2 years, extendable to a maximum of 3 years based on performance.
Applicant must be a society formed by the Central Government, State Government, or Union Territory Administration.
Applicant must be registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860.

For a new State Institute of Hotel Management (SIHM), the applicant must ensure transferred land is free of encumbrances and measures not less than five acres (two acres in hilly areas or the six specified large urban agglomerations).
The applicant must ensure the State Government/UT Administration commits to providing basic services/utilities (electricity, water, sewerage).

Land transfer documents must be in the name of the IHM Society, or if transfer is not possible, the land must be clearly demarcated and in possession of the State Government/UT Administration in the name of the Tourism Department.

Similar land and service requirements apply for new Food Craft Institutes (minimum three acres, one acre in hilly areas/large urban agglomerations) and for new centres of IITTM, ICI, NCHMCT (minimum five acres, two acres in hilly areas/large urban agglomerations).
For setting up an SIHM in an existing building, the building must be provided free‑of‑cost by the State Government/UT Administration and be suitable for housing the institute.
For upgradation of an existing FCI into an SIHM, the State Government must dissolve the existing FCI Society and form a new SIHM Society registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860.

For an Applied Training Centre (ATC) attached to a Central IHM, the applicant must be a Central Institute of Hotel Management and must have two acres of surplus land or ensure the State Government provides the additional land required, with no hotels within two kilometres of the proposed site.
Must be a registered society under Societies Registration Act 1860 or a public trust under Indian Trust Act 1882, and must have been functioning for at least three years.
Colleges and universities are eligible to apply.
Must have the capacity to undertake and promote research projects, including necessary facilities, resources, and personnel.
If the applicant is a college, it must be affiliated with a university.
Must not be receiving grants from any other source for similar purposes.
Colleges and universities must introduce aspects of Himalayan art and culture preservation in their curriculum or research courses, if not already done.
Applicant must have made a significant contribution to art and letters (traditional scholars with significant contributions are eligible even without published works).

Applicant must either be receiving a state pension of at least ₹500 per month or be recommended by the Zonal Cultural Centres, Ministry of Culture (for artists of their Member State where state pension is not available).
Applicant must not be receiving financial assistance under other Ministry schemes such as Repertory Grant.
Income calculation excludes any artiste pension assistance already received from the Government.
Applicant must be an Indian national currently residing in India.
Applicant must not be a Person of Indian Origin (PIO) or Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder.
Applicant must have the research proposal or project approved by the concerned University or Institute.
The proposed research must have a direct bearing on sports-related issues or contribute to the improvement of sports and games in India.
Applicant must either hold a permanent position in an institution or have a suitable arrangement with an institution.
The parent must certify via affidavit that they have a child exhibiting gender non‑conforming behavior.
The child’s age must be less than 18 years.

Applicant must be a Non-Government organization (NGO), institution of Central/State Government, Semi-Government institution, field functionary of State/Central Govt., Panchayati Raj institution (PRI), private sector forming cluster-specific SPV, corporate, or CSR foundation with expertise to undertake cluster development.

Cluster selection is based on geographical concentration of around 500 beneficiary families of artisans/micro-enterprises within one or two revenue subdivisions in a district (or contiguous districts), potential for growth in production and employment, and geographical distribution with at least 10% in the North Eastern region.
Applicant must be an Indian citizen.
Applicant must be a master craftsperson, either a National/State Awardee of exceptional standing or possess extraordinary skills and immense contribution to the handicrafts sector.
Applicant must have at least 20 years of experience in the handicrafts field as of 31 December of the previous year.
Applicant must have made significant contributions to the welfare and development of the craft and the craft community.
Selection considers excellence of craftsmanship (judged from samples, photographs, or videography).
Selection considers related achievements (bio‑data and supporting materials).
Special consideration may be given for languishing crafts, revival efforts, design innovation, and processing photographs of exhibits.

Applicant agency must be an NGO/Trust under the Indian Trusts Act, a Cooperative Society under the Societies Registration Act, a Firm registered under the Companies Act 1956/2013, or an Academic Institution accredited/affiliated to or recognized as a University or Deemed University by UGC Act.
If the applicant agency is an NGO, it must be registered on the DARPAN Platform-NITI Aayog and provide a Unique ID.
For NGOs/Voluntary organizations, documentary evidence (Work Order/Letter of Award/Contract) of undertaking a road safety programme or similar advocacy activity must be provided.

The applicant agency may apply individually or form a Joint Venture (JV) with another agency; a JV may have at most two members, who must appoint a Lead Member and agree to the terms jointly and severally.
Only projects involving road safety activities or advocacy/awareness on any social cause are considered for financial assistance.
Applicant agency must have completed at least one road safety or advocacy/awareness-related program in the last three years as of the proposal submission date.
Applicant agency must not have been blacklisted or debarred by any State or Central Government Entity from receiving funds.

Must be registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 or any relevant State/Union Territory Act, or be a public trust, or a charitable company licensed under Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956, or the Indian Red Cross Society/branches, or any other public body/institution with legal status.
Must have been registered for at least three years (this requirement may be waived in exceptional cases by the Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment).
For voluntary organizations, at least 60% of beneficiaries must be Scheduled Caste.
Other organizations or training institutions approved by the Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment are eligible.
Must have maintained and operated a bank account in the name of the NGO/VO for the last three years.
Must not operate for profit for any individual or body of individuals, except in the case of training institutions of repute.

Selection criteria include: at least two years of experience in the relevant field; aptitude and experience in welfare work for weaker sections; location of residential/non-residential school projects must be in Educationally Backward Blocks (EBBs) or service-deficient blocks with 40% SC population or backward districts identified by the Planning Commission or Integrated Action Plan Districts; financial viability to contribute its share and continue work without assistance; good reputation and credentials; capability to mobilize the community; networking with other institutions for optimum resource utilization.
Applicant organization must be a registered voluntary organization (VO)/NGO engaged in the welfare of Scheduled Tribes.

Must be registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860/State Society Registration/Public Trust or Institutions either under a statute or as a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, or any other act.
Must register with the NGO-Darpan portal of NITI Aayog.
Must have at least three years of experience running activities similar in size and objectives to the project for which grant is sought.
Must implement the project itself without passing the grants to another entity.
Must agree to comply with the terms and conditions and sign a MoU with the Ministry.
Must open an Aadhaar-linked bank account in its name under joint operation of the President and Secretary or authorized signatories, in an authorized scheduled bank.
Must have PAN and TAN numbers and have filed Income Tax Returns for at least the last three years.
Must be registered under section 12A of the Income Tax Act.

If you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, you can claim Child Benefit.
Child must be in full-time non-advanced education (>12 hrs/week supervised study) or an approved unpaid training scheme.
Child must be accepted onto the course before turning 19.
Child must not be receiving Universal Credit.

Child Benefit is not payable if the child is studying for a university degree, BTEC Higher National Certificate, pre-degree course (e.g., foundation diploma, access to HE), HNC/HND level 7, or CertHE.
Child Benefit is not payable if the child is on an apprenticeship, doing employer‑agreed training for a job, or training that is part of a job contract.

If the child leaves education/training, a 20‑week extension may be available if the child is aged 16‑17, works <24 hrs/week, does not receive certain benefits (e.g., Universal Credit), was entitled to CB immediately before leaving, and applies within 3 months.
Benefit applies if a child or the claimant dies.
The deceased child must be under 18 years old at the time of death.
The child must have died in England.
The applicant must be responsible for arranging the child's funeral (typically a parent or guardian).
Child for whom maintenance is sought must be under 16 years old, or under 20 if in approved education or training.
Applicant must live in the UK as their main home and have the right to reside there.
Applicant must be either a parent (no need to live with the child), a grandparent with main day-to-day care of the child, the child’s guardian, or a child over 12 years old living in Scotland.
Applicants who have no income and are either full-time students or in prison are not required to pay child maintenance and therefore do not need to apply.
Applicants cannot use the service if they have an existing court-approved consent order that is less than one year old.
If the child and the parent with main day-to-day care both live outside the UK, application is not possible.

Application is usually not possible if the parent without main day-to-day care lives and works outside the UK, except when that parent works abroad for certain British organisations (Civil Service, Diplomatic Service, armed forces, UK-based company/organisation, NHS, UK local authority).
Applicant must be a permanent resident of England.
Applicant must be a full-time student studying 120 credits or more in a year on a single course.
Applicant must receive (or be eligible for) student finance based on household income.
Applicant must not be receiving a Postgraduate Loan.
Neither applicant nor partner may claim Tax-Free Childcare, the childcare element of Working Tax Credit, or Universal Credit.
Neither applicant nor partner may receive help with childcare costs from the NHS.
Children included in the application must be financially dependent on the applicant.
Child's age must be under 15 years, or under 17 years if the child has special educational needs.
Childcare provider must be registered with the Ofsted Early Years Register or General Childcare Register.
From 1 August 2026, applicants cannot receive the grant if childcare is provided by a nanny.
Household income limits: less than £20,107.23 for one child, less than £28,914.47 for two or more children.
For injuries/illness due to service after 5 April 2005, must apply within 7 years of injury unless illness is a late onset illness.
For injuries/illness due to service before 6 April 2005, no time limit to claim but must be no longer serving in the armed forces.
Must have worked as a miner for British Coal or the National Coal Board.
Eligibility criteria vary by local council; generally aimed at those unable to afford essentials such as energy, water, food, or housing costs.
Some councils may limit household applications to one per year or distribute funds via local charities and community groups.
Must be diagnosed with diffuse mesothelioma.
Must have been exposed to asbestos in the United Kingdom.

For the 2008 scheme: must not be entitled to a payment under the 1979 Pneumoconiosis Act; must not have received payment from an employer, civil claim or elsewhere; must not be entitled to compensation from a Ministry of Defence scheme; must claim within 12 months of diagnosis.

For the Diffuse Mesothelioma Payment Scheme (DMPS): must have been diagnosed on or after 25 July 2012; mesothelioma must be caused by asbestos exposure while working in the UK; must be unable to trace the employer or their insurers; must not have made a civil claim against any employer or insurer; must not have received damages or a specified payment for mesothelioma and must not be eligible for such a payment; must claim within 3 years of diagnosis.
Can also claim as a dependent of a deceased sufferer.
Prior receipt of payment from the 2008 scheme or Pneumoconiosis Act does not disqualify but will be deducted from the DMPS amount.
Eligible to claim from both schemes; an unsuccessful DMPS claim does not bar a claim under the 2008 scheme.

The child must be living in England or Wales when claiming, unless they live in the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein (and only get help with daily living tasks), are abroad receiving medical treatment, or live with a parent working in the armed forces.

The child's disability must have caused the need for extra looking after or walking difficulties for at least 3 months and be expected to last at least 6 months, unless the child is nearing the end of life, in which case the 3‑month duration requirement does not apply.
At least one person living in the house must be disabled.
The applicant must intend to live in the property during the grant period (usually 5 years, but can be shorter).
The person submitting the application must be the owner, tenant, or landlord of the property.
The proposed work must be necessary and appropriate to meet the disabled person's needs.
The work must be reasonable and feasible, considering the age and condition of the property.
The work must be completed within 12 months of the grant being approved.
Work must not start before the council approves the application.
Separate planning permission and/or building regulations approval may be required.
The council may require a qualified architect or surveyor; grant funds can be used towards their fees.
Must be eligible for both a Tuition Fee Loan and a Maintenance Loan from Student Finance England
Not eligible if only eligible for a Tuition Fee Loan (tuition-fee-only funding)
Not eligible if eligible for NHS Disabled Students’ Allowance
Not eligible if receiving equivalent support from another funding source (e.g., university or social work bursary)
Not eligible if on a higher or degree apprenticeship course
Must be under State Pension age.
Must have worked as an employee or been self-employed and paid enough National Insurance contributions (usually in the last 2–3 years).
Cannot be receiving Jobseeker’s Allowance (JSA) or Statutory Sick Pay (SSP).
Applicant must be experiencing difficulty managing a benefit claim or State Pension (UK).
Service available for residents of England, Scotland, and Wales (Great Britain) only; not available in Northern Ireland.
Free TV licence if aged 75 or over and you (or your partner) receive Pension Credit.
50% discount on TV licence if you are registered blind (or live with a registered blind person).
Discounted TV licence for £7.50 if you live in an eligible residential care home, supported housing or sheltered accommodation and are either retired and over 60 or disabled.

Must be receiving (or have applied and awaiting decision for) one of the following benefits: Universal Credit, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit, or a Support for Mortgage Interest loan.

Must meet the relationship rules with the deceased: be the partner of the deceased; or parent of a baby stillborn after 24 weeks of pregnancy; or parent/person responsible for a deceased child under 16 (or under 20 and in approved education/training); or, if a close relative/friend, the deceased had no partner at death and the partner/parent cannot claim (e.g., lives abroad or is in prison).
Must be arranging a funeral in the UK, the European Economic Area (EEA), or Switzerland.
No specific eligibility restrictions mentioned; generally available to anyone requiring NHS prescriptions.
Help is only available for approved childcare.
Childcare vouchers are only available if you have already joined a scheme.
Free childcare entitlements apply to children aged 9 months to 4 years.
General help with childcare costs is available for children under 18.
Must be receiving Universal Credit
Must have take-home pay of at least £1 in the last monthly assessment period
Must be living in the UK, except Crown servants, members of the British armed forces, and their spouses or civil partners living overseas who may also apply

At least one of the child's parents must have been born in the UK, a European Economic Area (EEA) country, or Switzerland, or have lived in the UK since the age of 16 for at least 52 weeks in any 2‑year period.

If there is a surviving parent, eligibility requires either: (a) the surviving parent’s whereabouts unknown despite reasonable efforts to contact them; (b) the surviving parent will be in prison for at least 2 years from the date of death of the other parent; or (c) the surviving parent is in hospital by court order.
If you adopt the child, you may continue to receive Guardian’s Allowance only if you were already receiving it before the adoption.
Must have a job interview scheduled for a paid job, apprenticeship, or Department for Education supported internship in England, Scotland, or Wales.
Must reside in England, Scotland, or Wales (not the Channel Islands or Isle of Man).
Interview must not have already taken place.
Interview must not be for a volunteer role.
Must not be attending a job induction or job review.
To access the Jobcentre Plus Rapid Response Service, you must suspect you’re going to be made redundant, be during your notice period, or be within 13 weeks after being made redundant.
In Scotland, you may use PACE; in Wales, you may use ReAct; in Northern Ireland, a different service applies.

For New Style Jobseeker’s Allowance or Employment and Support Allowance, you must be under State Pension age, unemployed or working less than 16 hours a week, and have made sufficient National Insurance contributions (usually over the last 2–3 years).
Universal Credit eligibility requires you or your partner to be under State Pension age and have £16,000 or less in savings.
Pension Credit eligibility requires both you and your partner to have reached State Pension age, or one of you to be receiving Housing Benefit for people over State Pension age.
Must have a health condition or disability to be eligible for assessment under Universal Credit.
Must be pregnant more than 10 weeks or have a child under 4 years old.

Must either be receiving qualifying benefits, be under 18 and pregnant (no benefit required), or be a non‑British citizen with a British child under 4 whose family net income is £408 or less per month and who cannot claim public funds.
Not available to residents of Scotland.
Eligibility depends on age, income, residence, receipt of certain benefits, pregnancy status, and medical condition.
New claim only if you have reached State Pension age or you are in supported, sheltered or temporary housing.
Savings must be £16,000 or less unless you receive Guarantee Credit of Pension Credit.
Cannot be paying a mortgage on your own home.
Cannot be living in the home of a close relative.
Cannot already be claiming Universal Credit unless you are in temporary or supported housing.
Cannot live with a partner who is already claiming Housing Benefit.
Cannot be a full-time student.
Cannot be residing in the UK as a European Economic Area jobseeker.
Cannot be an asylum seeker or sponsored to be in the UK.
Cannot be subject to immigration control where your leave states you cannot claim public funds.
Cannot be a Crown Tenant.
If you have reached State Pension age but your live-in partner has not, you are ineligible unless you had an existing claim as a couple before 15 May 2019.
Scheme is closed; new claims for Income Support are not accepted.
Must have been employed or on an approved employment training scheme when the accident or disease occurred
The work accident or disease must have occurred in England, Scotland, or Wales
Cannot be self-employed
Must suffer from a disease or disability listed in the scheme (over 70 specified diseases) that is attributable to work
Must have worked as an employee and paid Class 1 National Insurance contributions (usually in the last 2–3 years).
Not eligible if self‑employed and only paid Class 2 NICs, unless working as a share fisherman or volunteer development worker.
Must be aged 18 or over.
Must be under the State Pension age.
Must reside in Great Britain (England, Scotland, Wales).
Must not work 16 or more hours per week.
Must not be involved in a trade dispute with employer.
Must not have an illness or disability that prevents you from working.
Savings (your own or your partner’s) do not affect eligibility.
To qualify, you must usually have paid Class 1 NICs for the previous 2 tax years; NI credits can count for one of those years.

If you previously received New Style JSA for the full 182‑day entitlement, you can claim again only after at least 12 weeks since the last entitlement ended and only if the new claim is in a different benefit year.
If you work while claiming, your earnings reduce the JSA amount.

If studying part‑time you may be eligible; if studying full‑time you may be eligible only if the course is at Level 4 or below, you receive no maintenance loan/grant/bursary, and you can meet the work‑related requirements agreed with your work coach.
You may claim Universal Credit alongside New Style JSA; JSA counts as income for UC and reduces the UC amount.
Must have been either registered as self-employed for at least 26 weeks in the 66 weeks before the baby's due date, or employed for at least 26 weeks in the same period.
If employed, must have earned £30 or more per week in at least 13 weeks of that employment (weeks need not be consecutive).

Alternatively, if doing unpaid work for a spouse or civil partner's business, must have done so for at least 26 weeks in the 66 weeks before the baby's due date, not been employed or self-employed during that period, and the spouse/civil partner must be registered as self-employed with HMRC and paying Class 2 National Insurance contributions.
Eligibility still possible if the baby is stillborn from the start of the 24th week of pregnancy or born alive at any point during the pregnancy.
Must give correct notice and proof of pregnancy.
Must have worked continuously for the same employer for at least 26 weeks up to the qualifying week (15th week before expected childbirth).
Not eligible if you go into police custody during the maternity pay period.
Not eligible for Statutory Maternity Leave if the child is obtained through surrogacy.

Must have stopped receiving income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Income Support, or income-related Employment and Support Allowance due to returning to work full-time, working more hours, or earning more money.
Must have claimed the qualifying benefit continuously for at least 26 weeks before stopping.
Must expect the new work or increased earnings to last for at least 5 weeks.
Must have been entitled to housing cost help before starting work and will still have housing costs when work starts.
Must be an ex-employee of the National Coal Board (NCB) or British Coal Corporation (BCC), or a widow/widower of such an ex-employee.
Allowance may be affected if you remarry, marry or move in with a partner (for widows, widowers and dependents only).
Allowance may be affected if ownership or tenancy of your property changes.
Allowance may be affected if you change your heating arrangements.
Allowance may be affected if who lives in your home changes (family or lodgers moving in).
Allowance may be affected if you take up employment or self-employment.
Baby must have been born on or after 6 April 2025
Baby must spend 7 or more consecutive days in neonatal care

Applicant must be the baby's parent or partner of the baby's mother and have caring responsibility for the baby (including adoptive parents upon placement or intended parents via surrogacy with parental order within 6 months)
Applicant must be taking the leave to care for the baby
Applicant must be classed as an employee and employed in England, Scotland or Wales

For Statutory Neonatal Care Pay (in addition to leave): applicant must have been continuously employed by the same employer for at least 26 weeks up to the qualifying week and earn on average £129 per week (before tax) over an 8‑week period
Must be classed as an employee.

Must have been continuously employed by the same employer for at least 26 weeks up to the relevant week (the week ending with a Saturday immediately before the week of the death or stillbirth) and remain employed up to the day of the child's death or stillbirth.
Must have average weekly earnings of at least £129 (gross) over an 8‑week period.
Must give the employer the required notice and information for Parental Bereavement Leave and/or Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay.

Must be the child's parent (biological, adoptive, or surrogate) or the partner of the parent, or have had day‑to‑day responsibility for a child who lived with you for 4 continuous weeks ending at the date of death (paid carers are excluded unless they are a foster parent paid by a local authority, reimbursed for expenses, or receiving payments under a will/trust).
Not eligible if another parent or a person with parental responsibility for the child also lived in the household.
For bereavements on or after 6 April 2026, different eligibility rules apply in Northern Ireland.
Must be named on the child's birth or adoption certificate or have or expect to have parental responsibility
Must not be self-employed or an agency worker/contractor
Must not be a foster parent unless they have secured parental responsibility through the courts
The child must be under 18

education_levels: course worth at least 120 credits for the year
other_conditions: Must be a student residing in England.
Must be taking time off to look after the child.
Must be the father, husband or partner of the mother (or adopter), the child's adopter, or the intended parent via surrogacy.
Must give the correct notice to the employer.
Must be employed by the employer up to the date of birth.
Must have been continuously employed by the same employer for at least 26 weeks up to the end of the qualifying week.
Must earn an average of at least £129 per week before tax.
Cannot have taken paid time off to attend adoption appointments.
Must reside in England, Scotland, or Wales.
Must have reached State Pension age (the exact age depends on your date of birth).
If you have a partner, you are eligible if either both you and your partner have reached State Pension age, or one of you is receiving Housing Benefit for people over State Pension age.

If you are from the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, or Liechtenstein, you generally need settled or pre‑settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (application deadline was 30 June 2021, with possible later applications).
Savings and investments over £10,000 reduce the amount of Pension Credit (every £500 over £10,000 counts as £1 weekly income) but do not disqualify you.

You cannot apply for Pension Credit if you are already outside Great Britain; you can continue to receive it for up to 4 weeks abroad (or up to 4 additional weeks if due to a close relative’s death), and up to 26 weeks if abroad for approved medical treatment or convalescence.
You cannot receive Pension Credit if you move away from Great Britain permanently.
Deferred personal or workplace pensions, and deferred State Pension, are counted as income for the assessment.
Certain benefits (e.g., Adult Disability Payment, Attendance Allowance, Child Benefit, Housing Benefit, etc.) are not counted as income for Pension Credit.
Must have a long-term physical or mental health condition or disability causing difficulty with daily living or mobility.
The difficulties must be expected to last at least 12 months from when they started.
Must have lived in England, Scotland or Wales for at least 2 of the last 3 years and be living in England or Wales when applying.
Receipt of Armed Forces Independence Payment disqualifies from PIP.
Receipt of Constant Attendance Allowance reduces the daily living component of PIP.
Receipt of War Pensioners’ Mobility Supplement disqualifies the mobility component of PIP.
If over State Pension age, a new claim is generally not allowed unless PIP or Adult Disability Payment was received in the last 12 months.
Special faster/higher-rate rules apply for terminal illness; separate guidance applies for those living abroad or non‑British citizens.
Illness or disability must be caused by a work-related accident or disease that occurred before 1 October 1990.
Cannot return to regular occupation.
Cannot do other work with the same level of earnings as regular occupation.
Leaving the UK to live abroad permanently may affect eligibility; temporary visits outside the EEA are usually allowed for up to 3 months.
Must show that self-employment is your main work (gainfully self-employed) by providing evidence such as tax returns, invoices, etc.
Must report self-employment income and expenses at the end of each monthly assessment period.
May be eligible for a 12-month start-up period during which the minimum income floor does not apply.
Must share responsibility for the child from birth (birth parents), placement date (adoption/fostering), or due date (surrogate).
Must not have started sharing responsibility after the child's birth.
Both parents must be employees (not workers) to qualify for Shared Parental Leave; workers may only qualify for Statutory Shared Parental Pay.
Must have been continuously employed by the same employer for at least 26 weeks by the relevant reference point (15th week before due date for birth parents; week of match for adoption/surrogate).
Must remain with the same employer until at least the week before starting Shared Parental Leave.
To receive Statutory Shared Parental Pay, each parent must earn on average at least £129 per week.
For the parent not taking leave, must have worked at least 26 weeks out of the 66 weeks before the relevant date and earned at least £390 in total in any 13 of those 66 weeks.
Must be classed as an employee (agency workers may also be entitled).
Must have done some work for the employer.
Must have been ill for at least one full working day.
Must not have already received the maximum entitlement of SSP (28 weeks).
Must not be currently receiving Statutory Maternity Pay.
If sickness periods are linked (each >1 day and ≤8 weeks apart), a continuous series lasting >3 years disqualifies eligibility.
If absent due to sickness for more than 7 consecutive days, a fit note must be provided to the employer.
Must have a mortgage or home improvement loan for the property you live in.

Can start receiving SMI from the date you start getting Pension Credit; after receiving Universal Credit for 3 consecutive months (or moved to UC within a month of another benefit ending and have 3 months total); you can apply from the date you start getting your benefit.
Must be applying for a benefit and need extra help to claim it (e.g., due to complex needs, disability, being a vulnerable young person, lack of support, or inability to claim otherwise).
Applicants living in Scotland are not eligible for the Sure Start Maternity Grant.
Applicant or partner must be receiving one of the following: income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, Universal Credit, or a Support for Mortgage Interest loan.

Applicants must usually have no other children under 16, except if they qualify under special circumstances such as expecting a multiple birth, caring for someone else's child over 12 months old, having refugee/humanitarian protection status, or claiming for a family member under 19 in approved education or training.

For refugees, humanitarian protection holders, or those who left Afghanistan after 15 August 2021 or were resident in Ukraine before 1 January 2022 and left after 24 February 2022, the grant is available for the first child born in the UK.
If claiming for a family member, that family member must be under 16, or aged 16‑19 and in approved full‑time education or training (as defined).
The baby must be less than 1 year old on the date of claim (applies to birth, adoption, or surrogate arrangements).
No new claims can be made for Child Tax Credit or Working Tax Credit; existing claimants must finalize their awards via the Annual Review letter.
Must live in the UK.
Must be under State Pension age.

If aged 16-17, may qualify only if meeting specific conditions: having a health condition/disability with medical evidence, caring for someone receiving a health/disability benefit, nearing end of life, being responsible for a child, living with a partner who is eligible for Universal Credit, being pregnant and expecting a baby within 11 weeks, having had a baby in the last 15 weeks, or lacking parental support.

Full-time students may qualify only if meeting any of the listed student conditions: partner eligible for Universal Credit, responsible for a child, having reached State Pension age with partner below State Pension age, having received a Migration Notice, being 21 or under studying up to A level or equivalent without parental support, studying part-time or on a course with no student loan/finance, or having a disability/health condition with certain benefits (PIP, DLA, Attendance Allowance, Armed Forces Independence Payment, ADP, CDP, PADP, SADLA).
Armed forces personnel stationed abroad may apply using a specific address.

The disability must have been caused by vaccination against one of the listed diseases (COVID-19, diphtheria, Hib, HPV, influenza (non-pandemic), measles, meningitis B, meningitis C, meningitis W, mumps, swine flu (up to 31 Aug 2010), whooping cough, pneumococcal infection, polio, rotavirus, rubella, smallpox (up to 1 Aug 1971), tetanus, TB).

Alternatively, eligibility may arise if the mother was vaccinated against one of the listed diseases while pregnant, or if the applicant had close physical contact with someone who received an oral polio vaccine.
Applications can be made on behalf of a deceased person who became severely disabled due to such vaccination, provided the applicant manages the estate.

The vaccination must normally have occurred before the applicant's 18th birthday, except for certain vaccines (COVID-19, polio, rubella, meningitis C, HPV, swine flu, meningitis W before age 26, influenza) or if given during a disease outbreak in the UK or Isle of Man.
The vaccination must have been administered in the UK or the Isle of Man, unless it was part of armed forces medical treatment.
The applicant's spouse, husband, wife or civil partner must have died as a result of service in HM Armed Forces or during war.
Partner must have died before 6 April 2017 for a new claim.
At the time of partner's death, the claimant must have been either married/in a civil partnership or living together as if married/in a civil partnership.
The deceased partner must have paid National Insurance contributions or died due to an accident at work or a work‑related disease.
The claimant must be under State Pension age.
The claimant must not have been divorced or have ended a civil partnership when the partner died.
The claimant must have been living with the partner at the time of the partner's death.
The claimant must not have remarried or formed a new civil partnership after the partner's death.
The claimant must not be living with another person as if married or in a civil partnership.
The claimant must not have been over State Pension age when the partner died.
The claimant must not be in prison.
The claimant must either be entitled to Child Benefit for at least one child or have been pregnant when the partner died (including after fertility treatment).
Must usually live in England, Wales or Northern Ireland (not living outside these areas).
Must not be only visiting England, Wales or Northern Ireland during the qualifying week (21-27 September 2026) while usually living elsewhere.
Must not have been in hospital receiving free treatment for the whole qualifying week and the preceding year.
Must not require permission to enter the UK with a condition that prohibits claiming public funds.
Must not have been in prison for the whole qualifying week.

If living in a care home, not eligible if receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit, or income-related Employment and Support Allowance and have lived in the care home continuously from 29 June 2026 or earlier.
